title: Route the 8 inline implemented||improved restatements through isFeatureDone
body:
## Summary
The feature-done rule (`implemented` OR `improved`) is restated inline at 8 sites instead of calling `isFeatureDone`, including `src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:39` in this context.

## Description
`src/lib/feature-done.ts:28` declares itself THE one done rule, but 8 sites re-spell the comparison: `src/hooks/useTabFeatures.ts:39`, `src/components/modules/core-engine/sub_ability/tags/AttributesSection.tsx:83`, `:111`, `src/components/modules/core-engine/unique-tabs/_shared/headers.tsx:21`, `src/components/modules/shared/FeatureMatrix/FeatureList.tsx:67`, `src/components/modules/shared/FeatureMatrix/VerificationSummaryBanner.tsx:9`, `src/lib/gdd-synthesizer.ts:178`, `src/lib/pof-bridge/verification-engine.ts:221`. They agree today; the file's own history (built features stuck as blockers because a reader counted only `implemented`) is the drift this invites. Fixed = every site calls `isFeatureDone` and a comment-stripped source-scan test forbids the inline pair outside feature-done.ts.

## Flow
- grep the inline implemented||improved pair across src -> 8 hits outside feature-done.ts
- add the source-scan guard (comments stripped), seed one restatement, watch it go red
- migrate the 8 sites to isFeatureDone; guard green

## Expected impact
Whoever changes the done rule changes it once; measured by the guard's count 8 -> 0. Same predicate, so nothing behavioural should break.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one done rule with no inline restatements
Before: 8 inline restatements outside src/lib/feature-done.ts (grep)
After: 0, pinned by a source-scan guard
Method: probe - grep count; the migration spans 5 contexts so this round did not build it
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: source-scan test (comments stripped) counting inline implemented||improved pairs outside src/lib/feature-done.ts; 8 -> 0

title: Make MODULE_PREREQUISITES exhaustive over SubModuleId like the wiring map
body:
## Summary
`MODULE_PREREQUISITES` has no entry for 5 of 37 modules, so 'no prerequisites' and 'never decided' read the same; the sibling `MODULE_WIRING_ASSETS` is exhaustive by test.

## Description
`src/lib/feature-definitions.ts:10` is `Partial<Record<SubModuleId, SubModuleId[]>>` with no entry for arpg-character, core-engine-plan, models, blueprint-transpiler, game-design-doc. `RecommendedNextBanner` branches on `!prereqs` (undefined) vs `[]` (`src/components/modules/shared/RecommendedNextBanner.tsx:121`). `MODULE_WIRING_ASSETS` solved the same problem with a coverage test that forces a decision for every new module (`src/__tests__/lib/feature-definitions-wiring.test.ts:22`). Fixed = an explicit entry (possibly []) for every SubModuleId, enforced by a derived test.

## Flow
- add a module to SUB_MODULE_IDS -> nothing forces a prerequisite decision
- fix: add the 5 entries and the derived coverage test

## Expected impact
A new module cannot ship without a prerequisite decision; measured by modules lacking an entry 5 -> 0. The blueprint-transpiler entry is a curriculum call the owner should confirm.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - every module has an explicit prerequisite decision
Before: 5 of 37 SubModuleIds have no MODULE_PREREQUISITES entry (derived probe)
After: 0 of 37, enforced by a coverage test
Method: probe - derived count over SUB_MODULE_IDS; not built because one entry (blueprint-transpiler) is a curriculum decision
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
src/lib/feature-definitions.ts:10
missing: arpg-character, core-engine-plan, models, blueprint-transpiler, game-design-doc
src/__tests__/lib/feature-definitions-wiring.test.ts:22 (the precedent)
instrument: derived test: SUB_MODULE_IDS.filter(id => !(id in MODULE_PREREQUISITES)) must be []; 5 -> 0

title: Reject checklist ids the registry does not declare at the moduleStore write
body:
## Summary
`toggleChecklistItem` / `setChecklistItem` accept any item id, so unknown or retired ids enter the persisted progress blob and the server row.

## Description
`src/stores/moduleStore.ts:181` and `:199` write `[itemId]: checked` for any string, and the project-progress POST unions `true`s and can never undo them (comment at `src/stores/moduleStore.ts:271`). Every counter has had to defend itself: `countChecklist` ignores unknown keys, and this round fixed `getRecommendedNextModules`, which did not (d4199184). Fixed = the write refuses (and logs) an id absent from `getModuleChecklist(moduleId)`, and loadProgress prunes unknown keys, so stale keys stop building up at the source.

## Flow
- call setChecklistItem('arpg-combat','nope',true) -> stored and POSTed
- fix: guard at the two writes and prune unknown keys in loadProgress
- measure unknown keys in a real project_progress blob before and after

## Expected impact
Stale keys stop reaching the DB, and a counter that forgets to filter can no longer be wrong. Could break callers or tests that tick synthetic ids.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - progress holds only registry ids
Before: writes accept any id (read in code); count of stale keys in real blobs not taken
After: 0 unknown keys after load/prune
Method: simulation - walked the two writes; the real figure needs the operator's ~/.pof/pof.db project_progress rows
Result: unmeasurable
Gate: none
evidence:
src/stores/moduleStore.ts:181
src/stores/moduleStore.ts:199
src/lib/checklist-progress.ts:24 (counter that already filters)
instrument: script over a copy of ~/.pof/pof.db counting project_progress checklist keys absent from SUB_MODULES; then a store test seeding an unknown id

title: Move the module auto-save debounce and history caps into shared constants
body:
## Summary
The 2000 ms progress auto-save debounce and the 200/100 per-module history/finding caps are literals, against the repo's UI_TIMEOUTS convention.

## Description
`src/services/ProjectModuleBridge.ts:94` passes `2000` to `createTimerLifecycle`; `src/stores/moduleStore.ts:160` caps history at 200 and `:261` findings at 100. CLAUDE.md says all timing values come from UI_TIMEOUTS in @/lib/constants.ts; UI_TIMEOUTS has no save/debounce key. Fixed = `UI_TIMEOUTS.progressAutoSave` plus named caps.

## Flow
- grep UI_TIMEOUTS for an autosave key -> none
- add the constant in src/lib/constants.ts (shared file) and reference it

## Expected impact
Save cadence is tuned in one place; no behaviour change. Touches the shared constants file.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - timing values from UI_TIMEOUTS
Before: 3 literals (1 timing, 2 caps) in context files
After: 0
Method: probe - grep; not built because src/lib/constants.ts is outside this context
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of literal timing/caps in the two files 3 -> 0 with tests green

title: Drop RecommendedNextBanner's local label and size helpers now the results carry them
body:
## Summary
`RecommendedNextBanner` re-implements `getModuleLabel` and a checklist-size map locally, although the registry exports the first and the results now carry the label.

## Description
`src/components/modules/shared/RecommendedNextBanner.tsx:16` builds sizes from SUB_MODULE_MAP and `:24` defines a private `getModuleLabel` identical to the one in `src/lib/module-registry.ts`. Since d4befb5e the results' `label` is the registry label, so `:138` can read `p.label`. Fixed = no local copies.

## Flow
- grep getModuleLabel definitions -> 2 (registry + banner)
- replace with the registry export / p.label

## Expected impact
One label rule; no visible change. The file is outside this round's paths.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one label lookup
Before: 2 definitions of getModuleLabel
After: 1
Method: probe - grep; out of this context's paths
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of getModuleLabel definitions 2 -> 1, banner tests green

title: Put DiskCheckPanel verdict chips on the status tokens
body:
## Summary
`DiskCheckPanel` colours its six verdict kinds and its action buttons with raw Tailwind palette classes instead of the status tokens its sibling panel uses.

## Description
`src/components/modules/shared/RoadmapChecklist/DiskCheckPanel.tsx:26-33` uses `text-green-400`, `text-yellow-400`, `text-red-400` (also on buttons and notes at `:85`, `:91`, `:152`, `:167`); the sibling `VerifyPreviewPanel` uses `STATUS_SUCCESS` / `statusBg` from `@/lib/chart-colors`. Raw palette classes do not follow theme tokens. Fixed = the chips read status tokens (or StatusToken), same hues.

## Flow
- grep raw text-(green|yellow|red)-400 in DiskCheckPanel -> 10 lines
- swap to status tokens; compare rendered colours

## Expected impact
Verdict colours follow the theme with the same meaning. A small visual diff is possible.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - status colours from tokens
Before: 10 lines with raw palette classes in DiskCheckPanel.tsx (grep -c)
After: 0
Method: probe - grep count; the round could not take the visual check
Result: better
Gate: none
instrument: grep count of raw palette classes -> 0 plus one rendered screenshot per theme
